'''Tara Elise Brendle''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|FRSE}} is an American mathematician who works in [[geometric group theory]], which involves the intersection of [[abstract algebra|algebra]] and [[low-dimensional topology]].  In particular, she studies mapping class group of surfaces, including [[braid group]]s, and their relationship to [[automorphism group]]s of [[free group]]s and [[arithmetic group]]s. She is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Glasgow]].{{r|glasgow}}

==Education and career==
Brendle received her B.S. in mathematics, magna cum laude, from [[Haverford College]] in 1995.{{r|cv}} At Haverford, she won All Middle-Atlantic Conference honors in 1992 for her [[volleyball]] playing,{{r|vb}} and won honorable mention in the 1995 [[Alice T. Schafer Prize|Alice T. Schafer Prize for Excellence in Mathematics by an Undergraduate Woman]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] for her undergraduate research in [[knot theory]].{{r|schafer}} She received her M.A.  in mathematics from [[Columbia University]] in 1996 and went on to complete her Ph.D. at Columbia under the supervision of [[Joan Birman]] in 2002.{{r|mg}}. After receiving her Ph.D. from Columbia, Brendle was a [[National Science Foundation]] VIGRE Assistant Professor at [[Cornell University]] and an assistant professor at [[Louisiana State University]].  She moved to her present position at the [[University of Glasgow]] in 2008.{{r|vita}}

Recent: 
* Elected Member of the Council of the London Mathematical Society (2014-20){{r|lms}}
* Member of the Scottish Government advisory group  Making Maths Count to oversee and drive forward policy and practice to transform Scotland into a maths-positive nation (2015-21){{r|frse}}
* President of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society (2023-25); Vice President (2025-26) {{r|ems}}

==Recognition==
Brendle became a member of the Young Academy of Scotland in 2014.{{r|yas}}
She was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2020 class, "for contributions to topology and geometry, for expository lectures, and for service to the profession aimed at the full participation of women in mathematics."{{r|fams}} She became a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2021,{{r|frse}} and in the same year won the [[Senior Whitehead Prize]] "for her fundamental work in geometric group theory, concentrating on the study of groups
arising in low-dimensional topology, and for her exemplary record of work in support of
mathematics and mathematicians". {{r|wp}} She was invited to give a Mary Cartwright Lecture in 2023.{{r|mcart}}
 
==Work==
In 2026, Brendle, with Vasudha Bharathram and [[Joan Birman]] posted a proof of the faithfulness of the [[Burau representation]] when n = 4 to [[arXiv]], whose status had not previously been known.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Barber |first=Gregory |date=2026-09-06 |title=The 92-Year-Old Mathematician and the Teenage Apprentice |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/06/science/92-year-old-mathematician-apprentice.html |access-date=2026-09-06 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> {{r|burau}}{{r|burausa}}
